source.quote: Exline from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1941.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Arthur W. Exline, senior power plant operative, Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1941". The end is recorded as December 31, 1941 (1941-12-31), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. EO 8967, signed December 11, 1941, cites this order by number ("Executive Order No. 8609 of ") and exempts the same employee again: "I hereby further exempt" ... "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942". It states no separate effective date, so its signature date is recorded as the event date. It is a later event, not an end: it is a new exemption for a later period and does not revoke, shorten or supersede the exemption in EO 8609.

in certificated aircraft is eligible for a

quirements hereinafter prescribed.

types of construction, of aircraft radio  
equipment which make the tests pre­
scribed by these regulations inapplicable  
may be subjected to such other tests as  
the Administrator may deem necessary  
to insure safe operation.
§  16.12 Waiver.  The tests prescribed

designed or constructed that such tests  
are not necessary to insure airworthiness.

Characteristics
§  16.30 Design and tests.  To be eli­
gible for type certification, aircraft radio  
equipment must be so designed and con­
structed that it will satisfactorily per­
form the function or functions for which  
it is intended to be used in aircraft under  
all flight conditions which may be met  
in regular service and must:
(a) Be free from hazard both in itself  
and in its method of operation;
(b) Be constructed of suitable and de­
pendable materials;
(c) Satisfactorily pass a visual inspec­
tion of the construction, layout, and  
electrical arrangement of all components  
of the particular aircraft radio equip­
ment and such electrical, humidity, tem­
perature, pressure, vibration, drop, and  
other tests as the Administrator may  
prescribe.
Inspections and Tests
§  16.40 General.  The prescribed In­
spections and tests shall be conducted  
by the applicant under the supervision  
of representatives of the Administrator  
at a designated time and place and in  
such manner and under such conditions  
as they may deem necessary.
§  16.41 Facuities.  All engineer­
ing, technical, and physical facilities  
which may be necessary for the conduct  
of all of the prescribed inspections and  
tests shall be provided by the applicant.
§  16.42 Report.  The applicant shall  
submit in duplicate a written report of  
the results of the prescribed inspections  
and tests which shall be in such detail  
as the Administrator may require.

§  16.52 List changes.  The holder of

ment shall keep all lists furnished the

vised lists containing all changes made  
subsequent to original certification.

§  40.235 Radio  equipment.  Appli­
cant shall show that each aircraft is  
equipped with a type certificated two-  
way radio telephone having sufficient  
power to permit communication, under  
normal operating conditions, with at  
least one ground station used or to be  
used by the applicant on the regular or  
alternate route, and capable of com­
munication with other aircraft of the  
applicant in flight. In addition, each  
aircraft shall be provided with at least  
one type certificated radio receiving sys­
tem capable of receiving radio range  
signals and weather broadcasts. Such  
receiving system shall include a type cer­
tificated audio filter system with suitable  
switching arrangements to be used in  
connection with the reception of simul­
taneous radio range and voice broad­
casts: Provided,  That such audio filter  
system will not be required if the airway  
or route traversed is not equipped with  
simultaneous type radio range stations.
3. By amending §  40.253 to read as fol­
lows:
§  40.253 Radio equipment.  Same as  
in §  40.235 and, in addition, applicant  
shall show that there is installed in each  
aircraft to be used in instrument or over-  
the-top operation (during day or night)  
over the proposed route, or part thereof,  
one additional separate type certificated  
radio receiving system capable of re­
ceiving radio range signals and weather  
broadcasts. Such receiver system shall  
normally operate from the main source  
of electrical supply of the aircraft but,  
in event of failure of the normal power  
source, shall be capable of being switched  
to operate from an independent power  
source. This system shall include an in­
dependent power source capable of oper­
ating such receiver continuously for a  
period of at least 4 hours. It is also re­
quired that such receiver operate from  
an independent antenna or from either  
of two antennas. Two sets of type cer­
tificated headphones and two type cer­
tificated microphones shall be carried in  
the aircraft at all times.
4. By striking the words “an approved”  
in §§ 40.2530 and 40.2531 and inserting in  
lieu thereof the words “a type certif­
icated”.

§  40.2532 Marker beacon receiver.  Ap­
plicant shall show that there is installed  
in each aircraft a type certificated ultra-  
high frequency receiving system operat­
ing on the frequency of 75 megacycles.  
The system shall provide means for the  
visual and aural indications of signals
transmitted by ultra-high frequency  
positive-cone-of-silence and fan type  
marker stations. The design of the sys­
tem shall preclude, insofar as possible,  
erroneous patterns of the transmitted  
signal caused by the receiving system.  
Such receiving system will not be required  
if the airway or route traversed is not  
equipped with ultra-high frequency posi­

stations.

EO 8613 is the order excusing Federal employees from duty on December 24, 1940. The held text is the official Federal Register issue of December 18, 1940 (5 FR 5143), as a machine text layer of the govinfo PDF; the order appears under its title with the trailing number line and the signature date December 16, 1940. The held text has two numbered paragraphs, so the inventory is two clauses: the closure and excusal for the stated day, and the direction to publish. Both are one-time commands performed on stated days: the closure on December 24, 1940 and publication in the issue dated December 18, 1940. The machine searches for the U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog record no hit that affects the order. The text layer is OCR; quotations below are limited to single lines and were checked against the held bytes.

source.quote: Emerson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1942.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Maurice A. Emerson, Chief, Division of Paper Custody, Bureau of the Public Debt, Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1942". The end is recorded as January 31, 1942 (1942-01-31), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. EO 9009, signed January 3, 1942, cites this order by number ("Executive Order No. 8615 of ") and exempts the same employee again: "I hereby further exempt" ... "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943". It states no separate effective date, so its signature date is recorded as the event date. It is a later event, not an end: it is a new exemption for a later period and does not revoke, shorten or supersede the exemption in EO 8615.

Mendenhall, Director, Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, who, during the month of February, 1941, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Walter C. Mendenhall from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending February 28, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by paragraph Eighth of subdivision  
SECOND of section 2 of the Civil Service  
Act '(22 Stat. 404), and section 1753  
of the Revised Statutes, it is hereby or­
dered as follows:
Any person who was on October 16,  
1936, an employee of the Rural Electri­
fication Administration established by  
Executive Order No. 7037 of May 11,1935,  
and who was not eligible to acquire a  
competitive classified civil-service status  
under Executive Order No. 74581  of Sep­
tember 26, 1936, because of insufficient  
length of sirvice prior to October 16,1936,  
and who has been employed continuously  
in the Rural Electrification Administra­
tion until the date of this order may  
now acquire such status: Provided,  (a)  
that he is unqualifiedly recommended to  
the Civil Service Commission by the Sec­
retary of Agriculture within six months  
subsequent to the effective date of this  
order; (b) that he shall pass such appro­
priate non-competitive tests of fitness as  
the Civil Service Commission may pre­
scribe; and (c) that he is a citizen of the  
United States and is not disqualified by  
any provision of section 3 of Civil Service  
Rule V or any other provision of the Civil  
Service Rules, or any provision of the  
Civil Service Act or any other statute or  
Executive order.
F ranklin  D R oosevelt
T he W hite  H ouse ,
January 14,1941.

[F. R. Doc. 41-38?^Filed, January 15, 1941;

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, and states when: "This order shall become effective at" "the close of business January 15, 1941". A one-time revocation is performed when it takes effect, so the command is spent at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The end is recorded as 1941-01-15.

research_rationale:
EO 8639 revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry. The held text is the official Federal Register page (6 FR 455, PDF pages 1-1) as a machine text layer; the page also carries other orders, and the clause span covers only this order from its enacting words to its effective-date sentence, under the heading naming Unalaska, Alaska and the number line. The order has one command, the revocation, with a stated effective time. It is a one-time command performed when it took effect at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The packet machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) record no hit affecting the order, and my scan of the held texts for the name Unalaska found no later order that re-designates or alters the port designation by this order's number. The text layer is OCR; quoted fragments are single lines checked against the held bytes.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: the order is a single revocation with a stated effective time, and no held text revokes or postpones it by number. Its own stated effective time, January 15, 1941, is the date the command was performed.","independent_command_check":"The effective-date sentence only times the single revocation and adds no command. No independent command remains after the revocation took effect.","savings_check":"The held text has no savings or continuing provision; the only surviving effect is the completed revocation.","scope_check":"One clause: the revocation of the designation of Unalaska, Alaska. The held page was read in full; the other orders printed on the page are separate instruments and are outside the clause span."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation was completed when the order took effect, and the resulting change, that Unalaska is no longer a designated customs port of entry under this order, is an accrued effect that does not depend on the order continuing to operate. The order has no savings clause.

NUMBER 22
Washington, Saturday, February 1, 1941
The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER
Revoking the  D esignation  of M olson , 
Washington , as a C ustoms  P ort of 
E ntry
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by section 1 of the act of August 1, 1914,  
38 Stat. 609, 623 (U.S.C., title 19, sec. 2),  
it is ordered that the designation of  
Molson, Washington, as a customs port of  
entry in Customs Collection District No.  
30 (Washington), be, and it is hereby,  
revoked.
This order shall become effective at the  
close of business January 31,1941.
F ranklin  D R oosevelt  
T he W hite  H ouse ,
January 29, 1941.
[No. 8654]
[F. R. Doc. 41-728; Filed, January 30, 1941;  
2:10 p. m.]

CHAPTER I—FARM CREDIT,.

RULES AND REGULATIONS GOVERNING EXTEN­
SION OF CREDIT BY WENATCHEE, WASHING­
TON, BRANCH OF REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL 
CREDIT CORPORATION OF SALT LAKE CITY, 
UTAH, TO FRUIT GROWERS IN OKANOGAN, 
CHELAN, DOUGLAS AND GRANT COUNTIES, 
WASHINGTON (KNOWN AS THE WEN AT-  
CHEE-OKANOGAN DISTRICT)  EFFECTIVE 
FEBRUARY 1, 1941
F ebruary 1,1941.
Pursuant to the authority of section  
201 (e) of the Emergency Relief and  
Construction Act of 1932, as amended  
(12 U.S.C. 1148) and Executive Order No.  
6084 (effective May 27,1 9 3 3 ), the follow­
ing rules and regulations are hereby pro­
mulgated:
§  95.1 Loans in the Wenatchee-Okan-  
ogan District, State of Washington,  
during 1941-1942 crop season.  The  
Wenatchee Branch of the Regional Agri­
cultural Credit Corporation of Salt Lake  
City, Utah, (hereinafter referred to as  
“the Wenatchee Branch”) is authorized  
to make loans during the 1941-1942 crop  
season to fruit growers in the Wenatchee-  
Okanogan District, in the State of Wash­
ington.
§  95.2 Eligible borrowers.  Farmers  
(including orchardists and fruit growers)  
are eligible to borrow from the corpora­
tion when they can qualify under the  
terms and conditions set forth herein and  
in the application and agreements re­
quired by the Wenatchee Branch to be  
executed in connection with such loans.  
Loans shall be made direct to borrowers  
and the Wenatchee Branch shall not dis­
count notes for any other financing in­
stitution. Borrowers shall be required to  
cooperate in such program or programs  
as may be promulgated by or developed  
in cooperation with the United States  
Department of Agriculture, and to com­
ply with Federal and state requirements  
now in effect or hereafter promulgated,  
with respect to sanitation, grading, pack­
ing and marketing of fruit.
§  95.3 Loan purposes.  Loans may be  
made to finance the production, harvest­
ing, packing, storing, and marketing of  
fruit, including the care and preserva­
tion of orchards as well as reasonable  
living expenses of the operator, under  
terms and conditions prescribed by the  
Wenatchee Branch Committee. Loans  
may be made also for the purchase and  
repair of equipment, for rehabilitation of  
orchards and for such other purposes as  
may be approved by the Wenatchee  
Branch Committee.
§  95.4 Applications.  Each application  
(to be presented in triplicate) for a sea­
son’ s financing shall be accompanied by  
figures for an operating budget. Appli­
cants will be required to agree to pursue  
approved agricultural and horticultural  
practices and to harvest, pack and mar­
ket their fruit in a manner and upon  
terms approved by the Wenatchee  
Branch.

research_rationale:
EO 8654 revokes the designation of Molson, Washington, as a customs port of entry. The held text is the official Federal Register page (6 FR 705, PDF pages 1-1) as a machine text layer; the page also carries other orders, and the clause span covers only this order from its enacting words to its effective-date sentence, under the heading naming Molson, Washington and the number line. The order has one command, the revocation, with a stated effective time. It is a one-time command performed when it took effect at the close of business on January 31, 1941. The packet machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) record no hit affecting the order, and my scan of the held texts for the name Molson found no later order that re-designates or alters the port designation by this order's number. The text layer is OCR; quoted fragments are single lines checked against the held bytes.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: the order is a single revocation with a stated effective time, and no held text revokes or postpones it by number. Its own stated effective time, January 31, 1941, is the date the command was performed.","independent_command_check":"The effective-date sentence only times the single revocation and adds no command. No independent command remains after the revocation took effect.","savings_check":"The held text has no savings or continuing provision; the only surviving effect is the completed revocation.","scope_check":"One clause: the revocation of the designation of Molson, Washington. The held page was read in full; the other orders printed on the page are separate instruments and are outside the clause span."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation was completed when the order took effect, and the resulting change, that Molson is no longer a designated customs port of entry under this order, is an accrued effect that does not depend on the order continuing to operate. The order has no savings clause.

source.quote: Ingling from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending April 30, 1942.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Clarence E. Ingling, Chief of Files, The White House Office, Executive Office of the President, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending April 30, 1942". The end is recorded as April 30, 1942 (1942-04-30), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. EO 9037, signed January 23, 1942, cites this order by number ("Executive Order No. 8670 of ") and exempts the same employee again: "I hereby further exempt" ... "for a period of one year ending April 30, 1943". It states no separate effective date, so its signature date is recorded as the event date. It is a later event, not an end: it is a new exemption for a later period and does not revoke, shorten or supersede the exemption in EO 8670.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 9031—Exemption of Edgar M. Cohee From Compulsory Retirement for Age; January 20, 1942; APP node 368015; common-crawl capture 2025-06-18T03:49:43Z
source.quote:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Edgar M. Cohee, chief office clerk, Office of the Collector of Internal Revenue, Los Angeles, California, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 8692 of February 21, 1941, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

January 20, 1942.

EO 9195 ends that command by naming it: it provides that its provisions are effective as of "June 1, 1942, and shall supersede" and the held OCR continues "amended by Executive Ordey No. 8706" "of March 6, 1941." EO 9195 was signed July 7, 1942 and published July 10, 1942; those dates are the alternative candidates because the supersession operates retroactively.

research_rationale:
EO 8706 amends paragraph 12 of Executive Order No. 5865 of June 27, 1932 (aerial-flight regulations). The held text is the official Federal Register issue of March 8, 1941 (6 FR 1333) as a machine text layer; the heading, number line and signature date March 6, 1941 agree. Its only command is the rewrite of paragraph 12. EO 9195, signed July 7, 1942 (7 FR 5257), ends it by express supersession: it states that its provisions are effective as of June 1, 1942 and supersede EO 5865 as amended by EO 8706, naming 8706. The first end is recorded as June 1, 1942, the effective date the superseding order states; the signing date July 7, 1942 and Federal Register publication July 10, 1942 are the alternative candidates because the effective date is retroactive. The OFR catalog search records the supersession by 9195 and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit. Paragraph 12 as rewritten reappears in EO 9195 with nurses added, an independent continuation of the substance. Quoted text is OCR, including the held spelling "Ordey".

The OFR catalog edge names only EO 9195 as acting on EO 8706, and my scan of held texts for \"No. 5865\" (cruden.py, 2026-11-04) found no other order amending or superseding paragraph 12 between March 1941 and EO 9195.","independent_command_check":"The rewritten paragraph 12 is the only command. Its substance reappears in EO 9195 as that order's own command, which is independent of EO 8706 after the supersession.","savings_check":"EO 9195 contains no sentence preserving EO 8706 as such; its paragraph 12 continues the substance independently, which is recorded as the savings basis.","scope_check":"One clause: the amendment of paragraph 12 of EO 5865. The held text was read in full; it contains the enacting words, the new text of paragraph 12 and the signature, and no other amendment."}

A commanding officer shall suspend", which reproduces the rule that EO 8706 had written into paragraph 12 and extends it to members of the Army Nurse Corps and Navy Nurse Corps. The substance therefore continues on the independent basis of EO 9195, not of EO 8706, which ended.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Ales Hrdlicka, Curator of Physical Anthropology in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending March 31, 1942". The recital says Ales Hrdlicka had been exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8058 of February 23, 1939, and No. 8368 of March 7, 1940; those earlier orders precede this one and are not events of it. The end is recorded as March 31, 1942 (1942-03-31), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Ales Hrdlicka, Curator of Physical Anthropology in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8058 of February 23, 1939, and No. 8368 of March 7, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Ales Hrdlicka from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending March 31, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

Subic Bay Naval Defensive Sea " ..., each followed by the establishing order, EO 8718 of March 22, 1941, and the operative words are "are hereby discontinued". operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the provisions of section 44 of the 
Criminal Code as amended (U.S.C., title 
18, sec. 96), and section 4 of the Air Com­
merce Act approved May 20, 1926 (44 
Stat. 568, 570; U.S.C., title 49, sec. 174), 
the territorial waters within Subic Bay, 
Philippine Islands, between extreme 
high-water mark and the sea and in and 
about the entrance channel within a line 
bearing true southwest extending three 
nautical miles from Panibatujan Point, 
a line bearing true southwest extend­
ing three nautical miles from Sanpaloc 
Point, and a line joining the seaward ex­
tremities of the above two bearing lines, 
are hereby set apart and reserved as a 
naval defensive sea area for purposes of 
the national defense, such area to be 
known as “Subic Bay Naval Defensive 
Sea Area”; and the airspace over the 
said territorial waters and over the Subic 
Bay Naval Reservation, Olongapo, Philip­
pine Islands, is hereby set apart and re­
served as a naval airspace reservation 
for purposes of the national defense, such 
reservation to be known as “Subic Bay 
Naval Airspace Reservation”.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the provisions of section 44 of the 
Criminal Code as amended (U.S.C., title 
18, sec. 96), the territorial waters be­
tween extreme high-water mark and the 
three-mile marine boundary adjacent to 
the eastern portion of Kodiak Island, 
Alaska, in and about Women’s Bay to 
the westward within a line bearing true 
north and south tangent to the eastern 
extremity of High Island, are hereby set 
apart and reserved as a naval defensive 
sea area for purposes of the national de­
fense, such area to be known as “Kodiak 
Island Naval Defensive Sea Area”.
At no time shall any vessel or other 
craft, other than public vessels of the 
United States, be navigated into Kodiak 
Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, unless 
authorized by the Secretary of the Navy.
The provisions of the preceding para­
graph shall be enforced by the Secretary 
of the Navy, with the cooperation of the 
local law enforcement officers of the 
United States and of the Territory of 
Alaska; and the Secretary of the Navy is 
hereby authorized to prescribe such regu­
lations as may be necessary to carry out 
such provisions.
Any person violating any of the pro­
visions of this order shall be subject to 
the penalties provided by section 44 of 
the Criminal Code as amended (U.S.C., 
title 18, sec. 96).
This order shall take effect ninety days 
after date hereof.

research_rationale:
EO 8718 establishes the Subic Bay Naval Defensive Sea Area and Subic Bay Naval Airspace Reservation in the Philippine Islands. The held text is the official Federal Register issue of March 26, 1941 (6 FR 1621) as a machine text layer; the page also prints the preceding Kodiak Island order and the following order, so the packet's single sole-paragraph clause (which ran through the table of contents and into the next order) is corrected to five clauses from the order's own paragraphs. EO 9720, signed May 8, 1946 and published May 10, 1946 (11 FR 5105), discontinues both the airspace reservation and the defensive sea area by naming EO 8718 for each, so every clause ends on May 8, 1946. The order states no separate effective date for 9720, so its signature date is recorded. The OFR-catalog hit for this order is the cross-reference from EO 9720; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit. The order's own effective-date sentence (ninety days after March 22, 1941) is part of the final clause. Quotations are single lines of the OCR text layer.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end found: the OFR edge and my scan of held texts for \"Subic Bay Naval\" and \"No. 8718\" (cruden.py, 2026-11-04) show only EO 9720 as an instrument discontinuing the areas; later orders printed beside EO 8718 in the 1941 issue merely repeat the penalty wording for their own areas.","independent_command_check":"Each clause concerns only the Subic Bay areas and each is discontinued with them by EO 9720; none rests on an authority outside the order that would survive the discontinuance.","savings_check":"EO 9720 has no savings clause; accrued statutory liability for past violations is the only residual effect and is stated to rest on the statutes.","scope_check":"Five clauses from the order's own paragraphs, each given its character span in the held text: designation of the areas; vessel prohibition; aircraft prohibition; enforcement and regulation authority; penalties with the effective-date sentence. The enforcement span includes table-of-contents text that the OCR layer interleaves in the middle of that sentence."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order states that violations of its provisions are punishable under section 44 of the Criminal Code and the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938. Liability for violations committed while the areas were in force rests on those statutes, not on a continuing command of the order; EO 9720 discontinues the areas and contains no sentence about past violations. No command of EO 8718 survives May 8, 1946.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Harry U. Wagner, assistant collector of customs, Denver, Colorado, Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending March 31, 1942". Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Harry U. Wagner, assistant collector of customs, Denver, Colorado, Treasury Department, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 8747—Exemption of Louis A. Simon From Compulsory Retirement for Age; April 28, 1941; APP node 371709; common-crawl capture 2025-11-07T21:09:04Z
source.quote: Simon from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending November 30, 1941.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Louis A. Simon, Supervising Architect of the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of six months ending November 30, 1941". The recital says Louis A. Simon had been exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling four years by Executive Orders No. 7581 of March 19, 1937, No. 7824 of February 25, 1938, No. 8046 of February 11, 1939, and No. 8369 of March 7, 1940; those earlier orders precede this one and are not events of it. The end is recorded as November 30, 1941 (1941-11-30), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Louis A. Simon, Supervising Architect of the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling four years by Executive Orders No. 7581 of March 19, 1937, No. 7824 of February 25, 1938, No. 8046 of February 11, 1939, and No. 8369 of March 7, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of six months:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending November 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order exempts Frank L. Hess, principal mineral technologist, Bureau of Mines, Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending September 30, 1942". The end is recorded as September 30, 1942 (1942-09-30), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Frank L. Hess, principal mineral technologist, Bureau of Mines, Department of the Interior, who, during the month of September, 1941, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Frank L. Hess from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
